o.text: From English trolley bus, ultimately via Russian тролле́йбус (trolléjbus).
Borrowed from Russian би́знес (bíznes), from English business.

From Proto-Turkic *keleŕ. Cognate with Mamluk-Kipchak كلاز (käläz), Khorezmian Turkic [script needed] (käläz) (in Qiṣaṣ al-ʾAnbiyā'), Chagatai كلاس (käläs), dialectal Turkish kelez, Kazakh келес (keles), Southern Altai келескен (kelesken).
Borrowed from Classical Persian تَجَاوُزْکَار (tajāwuzkār). By surface analysis, təcavüz + -kar.

From Proto-Turkic *yadag. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (yadaġ, “pedestrian, afoot”), Karakhanid [script needed] (yayaġ, “pedestrian, afoot”), Kazakh жаяу (jayaw, “pedestrian, afoot”), Turkish yaya (“pedestrian”), Uzbek yayov, etc.
